scope: Proposition 3.3 of the manuscript “Cycle--clique Ramsey numbers” (preprints/Cycle-clique-Ramsey-numbers-September-25-2026/Cycle-clique-Ramsey-numbers-September-25-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 189 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 366fc1d94b08e498), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 5. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let k ≥ 8 be an integer, set s = ⌊k/2⌋, and let G be a nonempty finite simple graph with α(G) ≤ k and |NG[I]| ≥ k|I| + 1 for every nonempty independent set I ⊆ V (G). Suppose that G contains no Ks. Fix a vertex r and a breadth-first spanning tree T of its component, rooted at r. Then there exist i ∈ {1, . . . , s} and an induced subgraph H of G, all of whose vertices have depth i in T, such that H is connected and nonbipartite, and |V (H)| ≥ k, δ(H) ≥ s, |NH[I]| ≥ s|I| (I ̸= ∅ independent in H). (3.2) The last inequality is strict whenever k is odd or H − NH[I] is nonempty.
